To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Thorough investigation and DOT with subsequent ambulatory blood pressure measurement is needed in workup of apparent TRH in tertiary care.

despite being a highly selected group of patients, referred for tertiary work up of apparent TRH in Oslo Renal Denervention (RDN) study, BP control was reached or secondary causes were revealed in almost two thirds.

despite being a highly selected group of patients, referred for tertiary work up of apparent treatment-resistant high blood pressure, almost two thirds achieved good blood pressure control or secondary causes were found.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevalence of true treatment-resistant hypertension (TRHT) in a population of apparent TRHT in a tertiary work-up.
the treatment of hypertension and its complications.
the prevalence and causes of treatment-resistant hypertension in a population referred from secondary to tertiary care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the prevalence of true treatment-resistant hypertension is 40–50% in patients with apparent treatment-resistant hypertension referred for tertiary workup, but that this figure is highly dependent on the selection criteria of the study population.
a large proportion of patients with apparent treatment-resistant hypertension can be cured or have a substantial reduction in blood pressure by thorough work-up and adherence counselling.

a substantial number of patients referred for tertiary work up of apparent TRH have secondary hypertension, white coat hypertension or poor drug adherence, and a significant proportion of patients with true TRH can achieve blood pressure control after a detailed investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the workup of apparent TRH is important to ensure that patients with true TRH are treated appropriately and to avoid unnecessary interventions.

a large proportion of patients referred for tertiary workup of TRH have either poor adherence, secondary hypertension or white coat hypertension, and that a substantial proportion of patients achieve BP control when investigated according to guidelines.
patients referred to tertiary care with apparent TRH should be investigated according to current guidelines and that 24ABPM should be performed after directly observed therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the majority of patients referred for RDN did not have true treatment-resistant hypertension, and that thorough investigation according to guidelines is needed in work up of apparent treatment-resistant patients.

a large proportion of patients referred for RDN did not have true treatment-resistant hypertension and that thorough medical investigation is needed in workup of apparent TRH in general practice and also secondary care.
a thorough medical investigation and DOT with 24ABPM are important in patients with apparent TRTH.
